# Data Source: stripe_identity_verification_report

The result of the checks of a Stripe Identity verification session. Look one up by its `id`. The checks hold the person's identity data, so `document`, `email`, `id_number`, `phone` and `selfie` are sensitive.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_identity_verification_report" "onboarding" {
  id = "vr_123"
}

output "document_status" {
  value     = data.stripe_identity_verification_report.onboarding.document.status
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the identity verification report to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `client_reference_id` - A string to reference this user. This can be a customer ID, a session ID, or similar, and can be used to reconcile this verification with your internal systems.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `document` - (Sensitive) Result from a document check See [`document`](#document) below.
* `email` - (Sensitive) Result from a email check See [`email`](#email) below.
* `id_number` - (Sensitive) Result from an id_number check See [`id_number`](#id_number) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `options` - See [`options`](#options) below.
* `phone` - (Sensitive) Result from a phone check See [`phone`](#phone) below.
* `selfie` - (Sensitive) Result from a selfie check See [`selfie`](#selfie) below.
* `type` - Type of report. Possible values: `document`, `id_number`, `verification_flow`.
* `verification_flow` - The configuration token of a verification flow from the dashboard.
* `verification_session` - ID of the VerificationSession that created this report.

<a id="document"></a>
### `document`

The `document` attribute supports:

* `address` - Address as it appears in the document. See [`document.address`](#document.address) below.
* `dob` - Date of birth as it appears in the document. See [`document.dob`](#document.dob) below.
* `error` - Details on the verification error. Present when status is `unverified`. See [`document.error`](#document.error) below.
* `expiration_date` - Expiration date of the document. See [`document.expiration_date`](#document.expiration_date) below.
* `files` - Array of [File](https://docs.stripe.com/api/files) ids containing images for this document.
* `first_name` - First name as it appears in the document.
* `issued_date` - Issued date of the document. See [`document.issued_date`](#document.issued_date) below.
* `issuing_country` - Issuing country of the document.
* `last_name` - Last name as it appears in the document.
* `number` - Document ID number.
* `sex` - Sex of the person in the document. Possible values: `[redacted]`, `female`, `male`, `unknown`.
* `status` - Status of this `document` check. Possible values: `unverified`, `verified`.
* `type` - Type of the document. Possible values: `driving_license`, `id_card`, `passport`.
* `unparsed_place_of_birth` - Place of birth as it appears in the document.
* `unparsed_sex` - Sex as it appears in the document.

<a id="document.address"></a>
### `document.address`

The `document.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="document.dob"></a>
### `document.dob`

The `document.dob` attribute supports:

* `day` - Numerical day between 1 and 31.
* `month` - Numerical month between 1 and 12.
* `year` - The four-digit year.

<a id="document.error"></a>
### `document.error`

The `document.error` attribute supports:

* `code` - A short machine-readable string giving the reason for the verification failure. Possible values: `document_expired`, `document_type_not_supported`, `document_unverified_other`.
* `reason` - A human-readable message giving the reason for the failure. These messages can be shown to your users.

<a id="document.expiration_date"></a>
### `document.expiration_date`

The `document.expiration_date` attribute supports:

* `day` - Numerical day between 1 and 31.
* `month` - Numerical month between 1 and 12.
* `year` - The four-digit year.

<a id="document.issued_date"></a>
### `document.issued_date`

The `document.issued_date` attribute supports:

* `day` - Numerical day between 1 and 31.
* `month` - Numerical month between 1 and 12.
* `year` - The four-digit year.

<a id="email"></a>
### `email`

The `email` attribute supports:

* `email` - Email to be verified.
* `error` - Details on the verification error. Present when status is `unverified`. See [`email.error`](#email.error) below.
* `status` - Status of this `email` check. Possible values: `unverified`, `verified`.

<a id="email.error"></a>
### `email.error`

The `email.error` attribute supports:

* `code` - A short machine-readable string giving the reason for the verification failure. Possible values: `email_unverified_other`, `email_verification_declined`.
* `reason` - A human-readable message giving the reason for the failure. These messages can be shown to your users.

<a id="id_number"></a>
### `id_number`

The `id_number` attribute supports:

* `dob` - Date of birth. See [`id_number.dob`](#id_number.dob) below.
* `error` - Details on the verification error. Present when status is `unverified`. See [`id_number.error`](#id_number.error) below.
* `first_name` - First name.
* `id_number` - ID number. When `id_number_type` is `us_ssn`, only the last 4 digits are present.
* `id_number_type` - Type of ID number. Possible values: `br_cpf`, `sg_nric`, `us_ssn`.
* `last_name` - Last name.
* `status` - Status of this `id_number` check. Possible values: `unverified`, `verified`.

<a id="id_number.dob"></a>
### `id_number.dob`

The `id_number.dob` attribute supports:

* `day` - Numerical day between 1 and 31.
* `month` - Numerical month between 1 and 12.
* `year` - The four-digit year.

<a id="id_number.error"></a>
### `id_number.error`

The `id_number.error` attribute supports:

* `code` - A short machine-readable string giving the reason for the verification failure. Possible values: `id_number_insufficient_document_data`, `id_number_mismatch`, `id_number_unverified_other`.
* `reason` - A human-readable message giving the reason for the failure. These messages can be shown to your users.

<a id="options"></a>
### `options`

The `options` attribute supports:

* `document` - See [`options.document`](#options.document) below.

<a id="options.document"></a>
### `options.document`

The `options.document` attribute supports:

* `allowed_types` - Array of strings of allowed identity document types. If the provided identity document isn’t one of the allowed types, the verification check will fail with a document_type_not_allowed error code.
* `require_id_number` - Collect an ID number and perform an [ID number check](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verification-checks?type=id-number) with the document’s extracted name and date of birth.
* `require_live_capture` - Disable image uploads, identity document images have to be captured using the device’s camera.
* `require_matching_selfie` - Capture a face image and perform a [selfie check](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verification-checks?type=selfie) comparing a photo ID and a picture of your user’s face. [Learn more](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/selfie).

<a id="phone"></a>
### `phone`

The `phone` attribute supports:

* `error` - Details on the verification error. Present when status is `unverified`. See [`phone.error`](#phone.error) below.
* `phone` - Phone to be verified.
* `status` - Status of this `phone` check. Possible values: `unverified`, `verified`.

<a id="phone.error"></a>
### `phone.error`

The `phone.error` attribute supports:

* `code` - A short machine-readable string giving the reason for the verification failure. Possible values: `phone_unverified_other`, `phone_verification_declined`.
* `reason` - A human-readable message giving the reason for the failure. These messages can be shown to your users.

<a id="selfie"></a>
### `selfie`

The `selfie` attribute supports:

* `document` - ID of the [File](https://docs.stripe.com/api/files) holding the image of the identity document used in this check.
* `error` - Details on the verification error. Present when status is `unverified`. See [`selfie.error`](#selfie.error) below.
* `selfie` - ID of the [File](https://docs.stripe.com/api/files) holding the image of the selfie used in this check.
* `status` - Status of this `selfie` check. Possible values: `unverified`, `verified`.

<a id="selfie.error"></a>
### `selfie.error`

The `selfie.error` attribute supports:

* `code` - A short machine-readable string giving the reason for the verification failure. Possible values: `selfie_document_missing_photo`, `selfie_face_mismatch`, `selfie_manipulated`, `selfie_unverified_other`.
* `reason` - A human-readable message giving the reason for the failure. These messages can be shown to your users.
